questions.stem: For a particle in a one-dimensional infinite square well, the ratio \(E_2/E_1\) is:

whyWrong.A: Square root of the correct factor.
whyWrong.C: Assumes \(E_n\propto n\) (like the harmonic oscillator spacing).

explanation.conceptTested: Energy levels of the infinite well
explanation.trapUsed: Mixing up box and oscillator spectra.
explanation.howToModify: Ask for the wavelength of the photon emitted in the 3→2 transition.

questions.stem: If the width of an infinite square well is doubled, the ground-state energy becomes:

explanation.whyCorrect: \(E_1 \propto 1/L^2\); doubling \(L\) reduces \(E_1\) by a factor 4 — less confinement, less kinetic energy.
explanation.howToModify: Ask how \(E_1\) changes if the mass is doubled too.
explanation.howToAvoid: More room → lower energy; check the exponent from \(E \propto 1/L^2\).

questions.stem: The number of nodes inside an infinite square well (excluding the walls) for the \(n\)-th energy eigenstate is:

explanation.whyCorrect: \(\sin(n\pi x/L)\) vanishes at \(x = jL/n\), \(j=1,\dots,n-1\) inside the well: \(n-1\) interior nodes. More nodes → more curvature → higher energy.

whyWrong.D: Counts one wall as a node.

explanation.howToModify: Ask for the number of radial nodes of the hydrogen 3s state (2).

questions.stem: A one-dimensional finite square well of depth \(V_0\) and width \(a\):

options.A: has bound states only if it is deeper than the particle's rest energy
options.B: has a bound state only if \(V_0 a^2\) exceeds a critical value
options.C: always has at least one bound state, however shallow

explanation.whyCorrect: In one dimension the even ground state always exists (the graphical solution always intersects at least once). In three dimensions, by contrast, a minimum depth is needed.

whyWrong.B: True for a spherical well in 3D, not for 1D.
whyWrong.D: Only an infinitely deep well has infinitely many bound states.

explanation.conceptTested: Bound states of the finite well
explanation.howToModify: Ask for the condition for a bound state in a 3D spherical well (\(V_0a^2 > \pi^2\hbar^2/8m\)).
explanation.howToAvoid: Remember the dimension: 1D and 2D always bind, 3D needs a threshold.

questions.stem: An electron is confined in a one-dimensional infinite well of width \(1.0\ \text{nm}\). Its ground-state energy is approximately:

whyWrong.B: Off by 10 — e.g. using \(L = 0.316\ \text{nm}\) or a slipped exponent.
whyWrong.C: Off by 10 in the other direction.

explanation.trapUsed: Power-of-ten slips with nm and Å.
explanation.howToModify: Ask for the wavelength of the 2→1 photon (≈ 1.1 μm).

questions.stem: For the \(n = 2\) state of a particle in an infinite well \(0 \le x \le L\), the probability density at \(x = L/2\) is:

explanation.whyCorrect: \(\psi_2 = \sqrt{2/L}\sin(2\pi x/L)\) vanishes at \(x = L/2\) — the centre is a node, though \(\langle x\rangle = L/2\) still holds by symmetry.

whyWrong.B: The average density \(1/L\) is not the local value.
whyWrong.C: Peak value of \(|\psi|^2\) at maxima, not at the node.

explanation.trapUsed: Confusing \(\langle x\rangle\) with the most probable position.
explanation.howToModify: Ask for the probability of finding the particle in the left quarter for \(n=2\) (1/4).
explanation.howToAvoid: Sketch the wave function before answering positional questions.
